answer: A farm therefore spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the anchor quota and the gale admission check. Admission is capped at 2 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. Because the orchard audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 10 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
